title: The groups behind the 42 homes, from their own reports
question: Which groups own these homes, according to the homes themselves, and how is the amount owed by related parties spread across them?
finding: 10 groups. PACS: 25 of the 42 homes, $431.4 million owed by related parties; its reports list up to 136 other facilities under the same ownership. Humangood: 2 homes, $228.3 million; Life Generations Healthcare: 4 homes, $179.2 million; Aspen Healthcare Services, LLC: 3 homes, $60.4 million; Telecare Corporation: 2 homes, $55.4 million. 34 of the 42 reports leave the parent's name (page 3.1 line 15) blank although they answer that the home is a subsidiary.
how: Group = the parent named on page 3.1 (1) line 15; where that line is blank, the home-office company named on page 10.4 (1) (PACS and PACS Home Office for the PACS homes). Other facilities = the list on page 3.1 (1) lines 40 onward, including a closing line such as '106 additional facilities'.
limits: The facility list counts every facility under common ownership, not only nursing homes. Not-for-profit continuing-care campuses (Humangood's) hold balances with their parent's obligated group as a matter of course. A blank parent line is a gap in the form, not a hidden owner: the same reports name the home office on page 10.4. Ownership through holding companies is not shown in these reports.
